GUIDELINES 2026/002
SUSTAINABILITY BOND GUIDELINES
ISSUED: 10™ JUNE 2026
IMPLEMENTATION OF THESE GUIDELINES
These Guidelines are intended to be used by any issuer of bonds or similar securities that wants
those securities to be identified in Papua New Guinea (PNG) as being Sustainability Bonds.
Those securities will have to comply with all necessary requirements for bonds of PNG securities
legislation including the Capital Market Act 2015, and any requirements for approval by
SCPNG prior to issuance. If the bonds are listed, the issuer will also have to comply with all
relevant obligations under the Listing Rules.
These guidelines are not issued as mandatory requirements in themselves. They are intended
to be incorporated by reference into specific bond frameworks, in which they will effectively
be mandatory. For example, it is recommended that they are considered for the following:
e Incorporation in whole or in part into a Framework for Sustainability Sovereign Bonds
of the PNG government, in which case the sovereign issuer will have chosen
voluntarily to incorporate them by reference, after which it will be obliged to follow
them.
° Incorporation into the Listing Rules of a relevant approved stock exchange, for any
bonds that are seeking listing or admission to trading on that exchange and wish to be
denominated as Sustainability Bonds or to use the word Sustainability in their title or
characteristics at all.
° Similarly, for any private bonds that wish to be issued by a PNG company, or issued to
investors in PNG, and to be denominated in some way as Sustainability Bonds, these

Such requirements must make reference to compliance with these guidelines as they are at

SCOPE OF THESE GUIDELINES
1.
An issuer wishing to issue bonds or similar instruments in Papua New Guinea, and to
describe them as Sustainability Bonds in the name of the instrument, or in the
prospectus or other bond documentation, will be required to comply with the
conditions set out in these Guidelines. Those conditions are signaled in these
Guidelines with the word “must”. Where something is described with the word
“recommended” or “may”, it is for consideration by the issuer but a decision to act
otherwise does not impact compliance with these Guidelines.
Descriptions of how a bond complies with these Guidelines may be set out in a
standalone sustainability bond framework for the issuer or the bonds, or may be
incorporated within other bond documentation, as the issuer considers appropriate.
In both cases, all descriptions and explanations should be clear and consistent.
INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL REVIEW REQUIREMENT:
3.
Prior to the issuance of Sustainability Bonds, the issuer must arrange for an
independent external review of the Sustainability Bonds, to give an opinion whether
their proposed terms of issuance comply with these Guidelines in relation to Use of
Proceeds and compliance with the eligibility criteria of the Guidelines, the Processes
for Project Evaluation and Selection, the Management of Proceeds, and External
Reporting. The person carrying out this review must be a registered company auditor
or meet the definition of expert as set out in Section 2 of the Capital Market Act 2015.7
That pre-issuance opinion, or a link to it, must be included within the bond
documentation, which must also specifically include the following:
(i) the scope of the review,
(ii) the identity, credentials, and experience of the independent expert,
(iii) any connections between the issuer and the independent expert, and
(iv) a statement that the expert has consented to the inclusion of their opinion in the
document.
USE OF PROCEEDS
5.
The issuer must ensure that all the proceeds obtained from issuance of the
Sustainability Bonds are utilized exclusively to finance or refinance ongoing projects
or new projects that meet the definition of what constitutes:
(i) an eligible green activity or project under the Green Bond Guidelines, and
1 Under the Capital Market Act 2015, “expert” means any person who holds himself out to be of a profession or
calling that gives authority to a statement made by him, and includes an accountant, lawyer, engineer, valuer,
quantity surveyor and geologist, but does not include a person acting in his capacity as an auditor or as a
director or officer of a body.

(ii) an eligible social activity or project under the Social Bond Guidelines.
The issuer must clearly state within the bond documentation the types of projects to
which the proceeds of the Sustainability Bonds will be allocated and how they meet
the above eligibility criteria. The issuer must also include a description of specific
projects that it has already identified for the proceeds, including the extent to which
those projects are to be refinanced.
Where the net proceeds of the Sustainability Bonds are to be used for refinancing
existing projects, the following details must be disclosed in the bond documentation:
(i) the estimated percentage of proceeds to be used for refinancing,
(ii) details of the type of project that is to be refinanced, and
(iii) the earliest date in the past to which the body corporate will look back in order to
identify assets/earlier disbursements that can be covered by allotments of
proceeds.
Projects financed through Sustainability Bonds may also be financed from sources
other than the Sustainability Bonds.
PROCESSES FOR PROJECT EVALUATION AND SELECTION
9.
10.
The issuer must describe the following clearly in the bond documentation:
(i) the sustainability objectives of the eligible projects, including the environmental
sustainability objectives and the social objectives,
(ii) the processes established for the evaluation and selection of projects to be
financed by the Sustainability Bonds, including the eligibility criteria used to
confirm that projects are eligible for financing and any taxonomies, standards or
certifications on which the criteria are based and, if applicable, any exclusion
criteria, and
(iii) any processes by which the issuer will identify and manage potentially material
environmental risks and social risks associated with the projects.
These processes and details must be established and disclosed within the bond
documentation before the issuance of the Sustainability Bonds.
MANAGEMENT OF PROCEEDS
11.
12.
KE
The issuer must also clearly describe in the bond documentation the processes it has
established to manage the proceeds raised by the Sustainability Bonds, including the
temporary placement of unallocated net proceeds.
Under those processes:

(i) The net proceeds of the Sustainability Bonds, or an amount equal to those net
proceeds, must be credited to a sub-account, moved to a sub-portfolio, or
otherwise separated from other funds of the issuer.
(ii) The issuer must monitor and track the allocation of the net proceeds to eligible
projects and to ensure that the records accurately reflect all allocations made.
This includes formal internal procedures to track and document the allocation of
proceeds to eligible projects.
(iii) The placement of unallocated net proceeds cannot include investment in loans to
connected corporate bodies, in illiquid assets, or in assets or activities that
effectively contradict the objectives of the Sustainability Bond. The bond
documentation must describe the investment mandate for the unallocated funds.
Where an issuer has more than one Sustainability Bond, the proceeds of the
Sustainability Bonds can be managed per bond (bond-by-bond approach) or on an
aggregated basis for multiple Sustainability Bonds (portfolio approach).
These processes and details must be established and disclosed within the bond
documentation before the issuance of the Sustainability Bonds.
REPORTING
15.
16.
17.
18.
19.
oN
The bond documentation must include a clear description of how the issuer proposes
to report on the Sustainability Bond.
The issuer must report to investors on at least an annual basis on the use of proceeds
until full allocation of the net proceeds. A copy of the report must also be filed with
the SCPNG and, where relevant, with the relevant approved stock exchange. !t is
recommended that it also report on a timely basis in case of material developments.
That report must include a list of the projects to which the net proceeds of the
Sustainability Bonds have been allocated, as well as a brief description of the projects,
details of any new projects since the last report, the amounts allocated to the projects,
and the percentage of the amount that is refinanced. it is recommended that the
details of projects include their actual or expected impact and the methodology
underlying the calculation of impact, including any important assumptions.
Where confidentiality agreements or competitive considerations limit the amount of
detail that can be made available on specific projects, or if there is a large number of
underlying projects making disclosure difficult, the body corporate may present the
information in generic terms or on an aggregated basis.
The report must include details of unutilized proceeds and their placement.

The issuer must arrange for an external auditor or third party to verify the amounts
allocated to projects and the unallocated amounts and the statements related to the
projects in the annual report. The issuer must disclose this in the annual report along
with the result of the verification, the scope of work, the qualifications, the experience
of the auditor or third party, and details of any relationship with the issuer. The person
carrying out this verification must be a registered company auditor or meet the
definition of expert as set out in Section 2 of the Capital Market Act 2015.
The issuer must make sure that any information required by these Guidelines is
available publicly at the time of issuance and throughout the tenure of the
Sustainability Bonds on a website that it designates and states clearly in the bond
documentation.

ISSUANCE OF GUIDELINES FOR GREEN BONDS, SOCIAL BONDS AND SUSTAINABILITY BONDS
In the exercise of powers conferred by Section 466(1) of the Capital Markets Act 2913, the Securities
Commission of Papua New Guines, hereby;
(a) Issue a Guideline that shall provide formal guidance on the issuance of Green Bonds on an
approved stock exchange,
(6) Issue a Guideline that shall provide formal guidance on the insuance of Social Bonds on an
approved stock exchange,
(¢) Issue Guideline that shall provide formal guidance on the issuance of Sustainability Bonds on an
approved stock exchange,
with effect on and from the date of publication of this instrument in the Notional Gazette.
Dated this Sth day of Junge, 2026.
